claims.statement: Having ready-to-eat items available takes the stress out of having to prepare something if you are not feeling well or are in a time crunch.

The 10 healing foods for flare-ups: hot/cold cereals (including oatmeal), white pasta, white rice, white bread, potatoes, bananas, avocado, poultry, fish, well-cooked skinless vegetables. The 10 foods to avoid during flares: whole nuts/seeds, popcorn, high-fiber foods (whole grains, brown rice, raw fruits/vegetables with skins), dairy, spicy foods, high-fat/fried foods, gas-causing foods (beans, l
claims.evidence_excerpt: Clinical dietetics consensus. The low-residue/low-fiber approach during acute IBD flares is standard practice. The "10 healing foods" list overlaps substantially with the traditional "BRAT" diet (bananas, rice, applesauce, toast) expanded for nutritional adequacy.

claims.statement: I recommend that you only eliminate one food (or a food grouping, like dairy or wheat) at a time. Eliminating multiple foods at a time makes it difficult to determine which food is bothering you.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Clinical dietetics practice standard. No trials comparing elimination strategies for Crohn's.

claims.statement: Two distinct one-week meal plans are provided: a "Meal Plan for Flare-Ups" (low-fiber, dairy-free, gentle foods) and a "Meal Plan for Remission" (more variety, more fiber, more protein sources). The flare plan emphasizes: oatmeal, white rice, white pasta, potatoes, poultry, fish, melon, banana, avocado, well-cooked vegetables. The remission plan adds: berries, peanut butter, eggs, pork, beef, tofu
claims.evidence_excerpt: Practical dietetics. No comparative trial data on meal planning vs. ad hoc eating in IBD.

claims.statement: You really need to take time off work/school during this period and treat the process like a healing vacation... The IBD Remission Diet is an intensive healing program and it takes a lot of energy for your body to heal itself... you have to rest and conserve your energy for healing work -- not other work.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Anecdotal: a patient who worked full-time while on the diet showed minimal improvement. Thompson attributes this to energy diversion from healing to work.
